misconceptions.claim: A rate k (s^-1) is the probability of the event happening in one unit of time (e.g. k=0.1/s means a 10% chance per second).
misconceptions.truth: A rate is probability per unit time only in the dt→0 limit (hazard): P(event in dt) = k dt. Over a finite interval Δt the probability is 1-e^{-kΔt}, which is ≈ kΔt only when kΔt ≪ 1.

evidence.note: Picked 'probability exactly 0.1 per 1 s' at 100% confidence during probe.
